unapproved_method_choices.name: 1. Development dependence estimator AR1_LAG1_AUTOCORRELATION_v1 and its mapping to the envelope (Track C item 1)
unapproved_method_choices.current_implementation: superiority.py L47 ESTIMATORS=('AR1_LAG1_AUTOCORRELATION_v1',). L228-241 computes the lag-1 sample autocorrelation sum((x_t-m)(x_{t-1}-m))/sum((x_t-m)^2) on ONE caller-supplied Development series (minimum 3 observations, L234). L249 sets the envelope point phi=min(max(phi_hat,0)+margin,0.99). One estimate per registry target is shared by all 8 cohort x control cells (L346-353). Which Development delta series (which cohort/control) feeds the estimate is neither specified nor preregistered.
alternatives: bias-corrected AR(1) (Kendall / Marriott-Pope: phi_hat + (1+3*phi_hat)/n)
upper one-sided confidence bound of phi instead of the point estimate
long-run-variance-ratio estimator on Development (Bartlett/Newey-West LRV / variance) mapped to the AR1-equivalent phi via (1+phi)/(1-phi)=ratio, which captures higher-lag and seasonal dependence
max of the estimate across all 8 cohort x control Development deltas, or a per-cell envelope
no Development estimate (fixed envelope only; package Q3 option B)
unapproved_method_choices.result_impact: It sets the Development envelope point, so it can flip FEASIBLE <-> NOT_RUN_INFEASIBLE. That decides whether CAL_VERIFY is consumed at all, and therefore whether a size-distorted STAT_PASS is possible. Direction: the current choice is ANTI-CONSERVATIVE at small Development samples and for dependence that is not AR(1)-shaped. Only the separately preregistered fixed envelope and margin offset this. Leaving the Development-series choice open lets a caller pick the least-dependent cell.
unapproved_method_choices.rationale: Track C chose the simplest deterministic, Development-only scalar that maps onto the AR1_GAUSSIAN envelope (Q3 requires a 'predefined' estimator). Track C flagged it as item 1, 'identity not chosen by the user' (gsup_implementation.md L30). The 0 floor is conservative for negative phi_hat. The 0.99 cap has no practical effect because size at phi>=0.97 is grossly infeasible.
unapproved_method_choices.evidence: EXECUTED synthetic probe, 2000 series per cell, mean phi_hat. True phi=0.0: -0.090 (n_dev=12), -0.043 (24), -0.024 (60), -0.011 (120). True phi=0.3: 0.116 / 0.210 / 0.260 / 0.282. True phi=0.6: 0.317 / 0.459 / 0.544 / 0.570. Seasonal process x_t=0.5*x_{t-4}+e (LRV/variance = 3.0, AR1-equivalent phi = 0.5): mean phi_hat at n_dev=60 is -0.049, which is floored to 0, so the dependence is invisible to the gate.

unapproved_method_choices.name: 2. Envelope process family AR1_GAUSSIAN only (Track C item 2)
unapproved_method_choices.current_implementation: superiority.py L220-225 accepts only {'kind':'AR1_GAUSSIAN','phi'} with 0<=phi<1. L255-262 _null_series generates Gaussian AR(1) innovations (x0=0, burn=50) scaled to unit variance. The boundary null is E[delta]=0.
alternatives: add Student-t innovations (e.g. t3/t5)
add GARCH(1,1) and AR+GARCH (as in the decision-package DGP grid)
add MA(q) / overlapping-horizon and AR(2)/seasonal shapes
use a Development-based null: block-resample the demeaned Development delta
a union of several families (all must pass)
unapproved_method_choices.result_impact: Determines FEASIBLE vs NOT_RUN_INFEASIBLE. Adding families can only make feasibility stricter (more NOT_RUN_INFEASIBLE, fewer CAL_VERIFY accesses). Keeping Gaussian AR(1) alone is optimistic for dependence shapes that phi does not summarise (seasonal lags, negative lag-1 with positive higher lags; see item 1). In the package §1 table, heavy tails and GARCH alone did not inflate M-B size at small n (n=12: iid .025, t3 .028, GARCH .020). MA(2) at n=8 gave .076, but an AR1 point at MA(2)'s lag-1 rho (2/3) would be more conservative. Caveat: those table values were produced with the simulation's convention, not the implemented one (items 3 and 4).
unapproved_method_choices.rationale: Simplest family whose single parameter is the Q3 scalar. Track C flagged it as item 2: 'heavy tails / GARCH / MA overlap not representable' (gsup_implementation.md L31).
unapproved_method_choices.evidence: Code: superiority.py L220-225, L255-262. Package §1 size table (decision package L31-42). Fidelity sub-issue (EXECUTED, analytic and synthetic): the burn=50 start understates Var(sqrt(n)*mean) by up to 33% at phi=0.99. That has no realistic verdict impact; see the autonomous item.

unapproved_method_choices.name: 3a. Degenerate bootstrap replicate counted as an exceedance (Track C item 3, part 1)
unapproved_method_choices.current_implementation: superiority.py L106-111: if the replicate variance v<=0 the replicate is counted as degenerate AND as an exceedance. The oracle mirrors this (evl_c8_gsup_oracle.py L43-45). The alpha-reachability check (L274) tests only 1/(B+1)<=alpha. The Q1 approval evidence used the OPPOSITE convention: simulation_source L35 scores a degenerate replicate as T*=-inf, i.e. never an exceedance.
alternatives: count as a non-exceedance (the convention of the Q1 approval simulation)
exclude from B: p=(r+1)/(B-deg+1), with alpha reachability re-checked on B-deg
cell NOT_RUN when the degenerate share exceeds a preregistered limit, or when n=2L
require at least 3 full blocks (n//L>=3) before the kernel may run
count degenerate replicates in alpha reachability, i.e. a pre-access floor check
unapproved_method_choices.result_impact: When n%L==0 a replicate is degenerate when every resampled block has the same start, with probability about (1/n)^(n/L-1). For n=2L (two full blocks) this puts a p-value floor of about 1/n, so STAT_PASS is unreachable for any alpha below about 1/n, even for a role that beats the control in every period. The feasibility gate checks size only, so it reports FEASIBLE (size about 0). The one-shot CAL_VERIFY is then consumed and the result is STAT_FAIL. Under the approved simulation's convention the same configuration is NOT_RUN (k-1=1<2 blocks), i.e. NOT_RUN_INFEASIBLE before access. A NOT_RUN_INFEASIBLE outcome therefore flips to STAT_FAIL, a false negative recorded as FAIL. For n//L>=3 the effect is small (floor (1/n)^(full-1)) and conservative. For n%L!=0 the event has probability 0 for continuous data.
unapproved_method_choices.rationale: Track C: conservative, so an undefined replicate can never support rejection (docstring L85; gsup_implementation.md L16 'ties and degenerate replicates count as exceedances (conservative)').
unapproved_method_choices.evidence: EXECUTED (synthetic, B=999, 20 continuous all-positive deltas 1+U(0,1)), implemented-kernel mean p / min p: n=4,L=2 .261/.238; n=6,L=3 .169/.111; n=8,L=4 .147/.118; n=10,L=5 .116/.074; n=12,L=6 .092/.065; n=16,L=8 .077/.052; n=20,L=10 .062/.037; n=24,L=12 .061/.036. With the exclude-from-B variant the mean p is .010-.030. The simulation convention gives NOT_RUN for all of these. Power at mu=0.8, alpha=.05 (R=500, B=199) for n=8,L=4 and n=12,L=6: implemented .000-.002; implemented blocks with non-exceedance .148-.280. EXECUTED end-to-end fixture (n=8, L=4, alpha=0.05, B=199, Provider mu=3.0): feasibility FEASIBLE (size 0.0), then STAT_FAIL; all 8 cell p-values 0.11-0.21, with 21/199 degenerate replicates in each cell.

unapproved_method_choices.name: 3b. Statistic ties counted as an exceedance (Track C item 3, part 2)
unapproved_method_choices.current_implementation: superiority.py L115: exceed += t >= statistic, i.e. r = #{T*_b >= T}, with p=(r+1)/(B+1).
alternatives: mid-p (ties count 1/2)
randomized tie-breaking
unapproved_method_choices.result_impact: Conservative. For continuous data the probability of a tie is 0. It can matter only for exact floating-point ties with discrete or rounded returns at tiny n. Mid-p or randomized tie-breaking would be a different p-value definition from the one Q6 approved.
unapproved_method_choices.rationale: Matches the standard Monte Carlo (r+1)/(B+1) definition approved in Q6 and the >= comparison used in the Q1 approval simulation (simulation_source L35: '>=TS').
unapproved_method_choices.evidence: superiority.py L115. Simulation source L35. Q6 in a6_method_approval.md L15. Any alternative would contradict the approved Q6 p-value definition rather than refine it.

unapproved_method_choices.name: 4. Studentizer: replicate variance uses n//L full blocks; original long-run variance uses all n overlapping circular blocks (Track C item 4)
unapproved_method_choices.current_implementation: Original: superiority.py L96-97 lrv = sum over the n circular block sums of (s-L*m)^2/(n*L). This part is identical to the simulation (simulation_source L25-26). Replicate: L92 and L106-107 use full=n//L leading blocks (including the last block when n%L==0), divisor full*L, centered at L*ms. The kernel runs if n//L>=2 (L93). The Q1 approval simulation instead used k-1=ceil(n/L)-1 leading blocks with divisor (k-1)*L and required k-1>=2 (simulation_source L23, L28, L34).
alternatives: use k-1=ceil(n/L)-1 blocks, exactly the variant whose size/power the user approved
keep n//L (current)
require n%L==0 and use all n/L blocks
include the partial block with a weight
use an overlapping estimator inside the replicate
a Götze-Künsch kernel-weighted original studentizer
unapproved_method_choices.result_impact: Identical whenever n%L!=0, since n//L equals ceil(n/L)-1 (verified: n=13, L=3 gave 0 decision flips across 2000 datasets). When n%L==0 the conventions differ. The implemented kernel is slightly more liberal and more powerful, and it RUNS at n=2L where the approved variant is NOT_RUN (combined with 3a this yields structural STAT_FAIL). The approved size table (package §1-§2) therefore does not exactly describe the implemented kernel for any grid cell where L divides n. Individual PASS/FAIL decisions flip on about 1-5% of datasets.
unapproved_method_choices.rationale: Track C: use every full block available to the replicate's studentizer (docstring L83-84 'se*_b from the replicate's full-block sums'). Flagged as item 4.
unapproved_method_choices.evidence: EXECUTED (synthetic, R=500 datasets per cell, B=199, same data and indices for both conventions; rates at alpha .05/.10). n=8,L=2, phi=0 null: impl .036/.088 vs approved-sim convention .028/.080. n=8,L=2, mu=.8 power: .388/.610 vs .370/.584 (21 flips at .05). n=12,L=3, mu=.8: .570/.780 vs .536/.764 (27 flips). n=24,L=4 null: .048/.080 vs .038/.082. n=12,L=4, phi=.3, mu=.8: .274/.576 vs .286/.554 (mixed direction). n=13,L=3: identical, 0 flips. The variant used in this probe reproduced G.studentized_cbb p-values and degenerate counts exactly on 8/8 cases.

unapproved_method_choices.name: 5. Seed convention: the decision seed is reused for every feasibility replication, and the same seed and index set are used for all 8 cells (Track C item 5)
unapproved_method_choices.current_implementation: superiority.py L288-289 calls studentized_cbb(..., seed=s['seed']) in every feasibility replication, so bootstrap indices are identical across replications. L284 derives the per-envelope-point null-data RNG as Random(int(digest([feasibility_seed, point])[:16],16)). L415 uses the same decision seed, and hence the same index set, for all 8 cohort x control cells.
alternatives: independent per-replication bootstrap seeds derived from the feasibility seed (estimates the unconditional size of the procedure)
report both conditional (current) and unconditional size and gate on the worse of the two
per-cell decision seeds derived from one registered master seed
a fixed published derivation rule (e.g. SHA-256 of seed||cell||replication)
unapproved_method_choices.result_impact: The feasibility verdict depends on the decision-seed value, so FEASIBLE <-> NOT_RUN_INFEASIBLE can flip with the seed alone. Together with the campaign_id re-registration loophole this enables seed shopping. Sharing one index set across cells correlates the cells' decisions but does not change per-cell size under the IUT. The realised p-values, and so marginal decisions, change with the derivation rule. A6-S4 lists 'seed convention' as something to fix before CAL_VERIFY, but no convention has been approved.
unapproved_method_choices.rationale: Track C: assess size 'under the exact registered procedure' (docstring L266-268), i.e. conditional on the exact index set that will later be applied to CAL_VERIFY. Flagged as item 5.
unapproved_method_choices.evidence: EXECUTED (fixture scope: alpha=.10, tolerance=.05, n=24, L=3, B=99, R=200, feasibility seed 11; decision seeds 1-12). Envelope phi=.3: sizes .09-.12, 12/12 FEASIBLE. phi=.45: sizes .12-.155, 11/12 FEASIBLE. phi=.6: sizes .145-.185, 2/12 FEASIBLE. The spread is of the order of the Monte Carlo SE at R=200 (about .026).

unapproved_method_choices.name: 6. Feasibility criterion form: size-only point estimate; no power condition; undefined replications kept in the denominator
unapproved_method_choices.current_implementation: superiority.py L293-298: within_tolerance = empirical_size <= alpha + size_tolerance, compared as a point estimate with no Monte Carlo uncertainty bound. There is no power requirement. Replications whose statistic is undefined (MissingStatisticalEvidence) are counted in the denominator as non-rejections (L290-294). Pre-checks at L274-279: alpha reachability 1/(B+1), minimum support, at least 2 full blocks.
alternatives: add a minimum-power condition at a preregistered effect size (the package Q2 option A text mentions 'size and power')
gate on an upper confidence bound of empirical size instead of the point estimate
exclude undefined replications from the denominator, or treat them as rejections
an effective-alpha reachability check that includes the degenerate floor (item 3a)
unapproved_method_choices.result_impact: With a size-only gate, powerless configurations (n=2L; very large L at small n) pass as FEASIBLE and consume the one-shot CAL_VERIFY, producing an uninformative STAT_FAIL. A power condition would turn these into NOT_RUN_INFEASIBLE before access. A confidence-bound criterion makes marginal configurations INFEASIBLE more often (more conservative). Under the current AR1_GAUSSIAN family the undefined-count choice has practically no impact: zero long-run variance has probability 0 for Gaussian data, and block-count failures are pre-checked.
unapproved_method_choices.rationale: This is the literal reading of the Q2/Q4 approval: 'If the simulated size exceeds the preregistered tolerance ... NOT_RUN_INFEASIBLE'. The approval record lists power only among numeric/evidence items ('power/feasibility evidence', a6_method_approval.md L17-18).
unapproved_method_choices.evidence: superiority.py L274-298. Decision package L149 and L153 (approval sentence for size; the power wording appears only in the option description). End-to-end probe in item 3a (FEASIBLE, then STAT_FAIL).

unapproved_method_choices.name: 7. A6-S5 remnant: cell-status aggregation precedence (NOT_RUN over STAT_FAIL) and undefined cells
unapproved_method_choices.current_implementation: superiority.py L381-387: if ANY cell is NOT_RUN the overall status is NOT_RUN, even when another well-defined cell is NOT_REJECTED. L98-99 and L416-418: a zero original long-run variance (e.g. role identical to a control, or a constant delta of either sign) makes the cell NOT_RUN.
alternatives: STAT_FAIL takes precedence whenever a well-defined cell is NOT_REJECTED, because the conjunction is already falsified
report both: statistical_status=STAT_FAIL with incomplete_cells listed
classify role==control identity (delta identically 0) as IntegrityFailure/FAIL rather than NOT_RUN
unapproved_method_choices.result_impact: Flips the reported result between NOT_RUN and STAT_FAIL. The flip does not affect STAT_PASS, which still requires every cell to reject.
unapproved_method_choices.rationale: Fail-closed to NOT_RUN for any undefined evidence, consistent with the C6/C7 rule 'legitimate undefined support = NOT_RUN'.
unapproved_method_choices.evidence: EXECUTED probe: one cell with delta identically 0 (EQUAL_SIMPLE set equal to role) and MARKET_CAP cells failing gave cell statuses {NOT_REJECTED, NOT_RUN, REJECT_H0} and overall status NOT_RUN.

unapproved_method_choices.name: 8. A6-S4/S5 remnant: statistic family and return basis binding
unapproved_method_choices.current_implementation: superiority.py L46 EVIDENCE_KIND='CONTROL_RELATIVE_PERIOD_NET_RETURN_DIFFERENCE'. L412 delta=role-control per period. One-sided H0: E[delta]<=0, 'GREATER' (L119). This follows decision package §0 ('Δ_t = net(role) − net(control) ... one-sided H0: μ_Δ ≤ 0'), which Q1 approved by reference. However, the provider series are not bound to an exact C3 path (e.g. NET_OF_TRADING_COST_PRE_TAX), and no real provider exists.
alternatives: net pre-tax arithmetic period difference (current)
real or RF-relative period difference
log-return difference
a CAGR/relative-wealth basis aligned with the A9 economic units
unapproved_method_choices.result_impact: A different delta definition changes every cell statistic, so PASS/FAIL can flip. The S7 effect-floor unit and the A9 premium/opportunity units must also be consistent with this basis.
unapproved_method_choices.rationale: Q1 package definition. The arithmetic mean difference is what a bootstrap-t of the mean tests.
unapproved_method_choices.evidence: Decision package L24. superiority.py L46, L412. The A6 partial approval S4 lists 'statistic family' as fixed pre-access. The approval record names only the method ID, so the C3 path identity still needs explicit confirmation when the real provider is built.

unapproved_method_choices.name: 9. Q5 deterministic block rule form
unapproved_method_choices.current_implementation: superiority.py L141-142: block_rule kind DETERMINISTIC_RULE raises MissingPrerequisite ('no deterministic block rule is approved yet'). Only FIXED is usable. Data-driven selection raises IntegrityFailure (L143).
alternatives: a single fixed L (Q5 option A)
L=ceil(c*n^(1/3)) or a similar f(n) with a registered coefficient (Q5 option B)
